newsitem.title: NIGERIA: SOCCER-TWO FRENCHMEN CONSIDERED AS NIGERIA TEAM BOSS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TWO FRENCHMEN CONSIDERED AS NIGERIA TEAM BOSS.

text.p: Frenchmen Claude Leroy and Phillipe Troussier, who both coached other African national teams, have been included on the shortlist to take over as Nigeria's national team manager, it was announced on Monday.

Sports ministry official Mainassara Ilo said the two Frenchmen were among several candidates being considered for the post following the dismissal of Amodu Shaibu as national team coach earlier in the day. The successful applicant would be named by February 15, he said.
A Nigerian, Monday Sinclair, was appointed as the team coach and he would work under the new manager, Ilo said.
Shaibu's dismissal for "gross misconduct" was announced earlier.

"The Nigeria Football Association (NFA) has sacked Amodu Shaibu for gross misconduct, insubordination and making embarrassing remarks about its activities and the person of the sports minister," NFA spokesman Austin Mgbolu said.
Shaibu had been placed in temporary charge of the national squad in October while a permanent replacement was sought for former manager Jo Bonfrere.
The Dutchman quit the job alleging poor treatment and interference in his duties by the sports authorities.
Of the two French candidates, Ilo said: "Leroy and Troussier know African soccer inside out."

Leroy was the Cameroon coach when they won the African Cup of Nations in 1988 while Troussier was coach of Ivorien clubside ASEC Mimosas and also trained the national team in 1993. He lost his job after failing to take the Ivory Coast for the 1994 World Cup from the group from which Nigeria qualified.
Nigeria, current Olympic champions, host Guinea on April 5 in their next World Cup qualifier.
